event_description: Historical context — Optus nationwide outage interrupted access to Triple Zero. The regulator later published findings on access failures and missed welfare checks.
Historical context — Communications Minister records Optus’s revised unsuccessful mobile-call count, retaining the original figure and the revised minimum.
Historical context — Richard Bean’s final review records emergency-call fallback and the limits of remote intervention during the Optus outage.

Historical context — CrowdStrike’s signed filing dates update release to 04:09 and reversion to 05:27 Coordinated Universal Time. Google Cloud reports customer-system symptoms from 04:09. Reversion did not mark completion of customer restoration.
Historical context — Australia’s cyber agency publishes its advisory on widespread Windows disruption.
Historical context — Australia’s consumer regulator issues the outage-related scam warning; the cyber agency reports material presented as recovery assistance.
Historical context — Microsoft publishes a global device estimate and its account of recovery coordination. Its 18 July reference has an unspecified time zone.
Historical context — The Australian Broadcasting Corporation publishes Lucas Gibson’s firsthand account of unavailable airport service-desk assistance.
Historical context — Published interview records Leon Wilson’s account of being stranded in Osaka and incurring upfront expenses.
Historical context — CrowdStrike executive Adam Meyers testifies on the outage and customer recovery. A later bounded transcript search did not locate the deployment minute.
Historical context — Communications regulator publishes emergency-access and welfare-check figures for the 2023 Optus outage. Its access count measures people.
Historical context — The Australian Signals Directorate’s annual report describes outage-themed impersonation and defensive measures. Exact case-study publication day remains unverified here.
Google reports disruption to Security Operations searches, detections and dashboards from 14:07 to 22:30 Pacific time. Third-party network attribution remains the operator’s account.
Microsoft 365 tenant notices reproduced by the University of Pennsylvania report an incident start at 16:20 Coordinated Universal Time.
Microsoft 365 tenant notices report a 16:10 Coordinated Universal Time incident end. Local recovery times can differ.

The Federal Aviation Administration says a nationwide ground stop followed technical disruption starting at about 15:30 Eastern Time. Secretary Duffy confirms the airspace reopened at 20:15 Eastern Time.
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports observing Microsoft 365 outage-themed phishing. Successful credential capture, malware delivery and subsequent compromise were unconfirmed in its report.
University of Queensland posts a local Microsoft 365 incident at 04:27 Australian Eastern Standard Time, distinct from the provider’s incident interval.
Washington University publishes manual timekeeping instructions for employees and student workers during the Workday outage and marks its local incident resolved at 18:49 Central Standard Time.
University of Queensland marks its local Microsoft 365 incident resolved at 14:17 Australian Eastern Standard Time.
United chief executive Scott Kirby publicly reports effects on its operations, employees and customers from the nationwide ground stop.
Federal Aviation Administration publishes its ground stop account and gives a daily cancellation estimate. It says some cancellations were not directly caused by the ground stop.
United Kingdom minister Ian Murray reports Microsoft 365 disruption to health and other public services and states emergency services remained operational.
Niagara Frontier Transportation Authority briefing records airport-specific arrival and departure cancellations for 13–16 November.
Australian Prudential Regulation Authority Deputy Chair reports customer and entity disruptions and says critical financial services continued.
The agriculture department publishes a messaging disruption update with alternate cargo lodgement and states that Integrated Cargo System Self Assessed Clearance evaluations continued.
The agriculture department issues its messaging restoration notice. Completion of delayed individual transactions remains unverified.
The agriculture department cancels the planned multiple-system outages for 13–15 November. The messaging disruption was reported separately.
A third-party hosted copy of a Microsoft post-incident report bears this date and distinguishes active impact, backlog recovery and final customer communication.
Washington University publishes alternative workflows for Microsoft 365 degradation, including a fallback for time-sensitive patient communication.
Plaid publishes a partial-outage notice concerning Chase connections and later marks the Plaid incident resolved.
Chase spokesperson publicly gives the bank’s technical explanation. An affected provider records intermittent connection errors separately.
A freight forwarder advertised a planned Brisbane terminal outage for 20 November. Whether and when the terminal actually stopped operating remains pending.
Chase publicly reports a separate vendor incident with potential marketing-data exposure. It says it found no connection to earlier service disruptions.
The Australian agriculture department reports its cargo lodgement service unavailable as of 10:30 Australian Eastern Daylight Time.
The Australian agriculture department reports four import and reporting systems restored at 18:40 Australian Eastern Daylight Time.
Brown University publishes alternate time-reporting arrangements during local Workday unavailability.
Brown University marks its Workday incident resolved at 12:28 Eastern Standard Time and reports automated processing catching up.
A healthcare trust suspends its online musculoskeletal self-referral route and later reports referral systems returning to normal.
King’s College Hospital trust reports that Microsoft services have been restored and its operations are normal.
A named passenger account from Charlotte documents an onboard announcement during the nationwide ground stop and the report describes subsequent deplaning.
The agriculture department reports cargo lodgement disruption as of about 07:36 Australian Eastern Daylight Time and warns that users may see errors.
The agriculture department reports cargo lodgement access restored at 09:51 Australian Eastern Daylight Time.

An uncorrected Tasmanian parliamentary proof records a question about Microsoft provider dependence and business impacts, and the minister’s reported position that no cyber matter had been indicated to his knowledge.
At 10:30 the Essex care board reported that the Microsoft outage was affecting digital communications and provided a temporary telephone route for urgent provider referrals.
At 16:00 the Essex care board reported that email was beginning to recover unevenly and told senders of unacknowledged urgent referrals to confirm receipt.
East Midlands Ambulance Service reported its emergency service was unaffected, while non-emergency transport phone lines were busier and staff used contingency communications.
South East Coast Ambulance Service reported Microsoft communications disruption but said call triage and ambulance dispatch remained operational.
At 15:47 UTC GitHub opened a pull-request degradation incident. Its saved feed records resolution at 18:29 UTC; the presently visible resolved update was modified on 23 November.
At 20:14 UTC GitHub attributed degraded Copilot model availability to an upstream provider and suggested alternative model selection; it reported resolution at 21:27 UTC.
At 11:59 UTC GitHub opened a second pull-request degradation incident and reported resolution at 16:26 UTC; the presently visible resolved update was modified on 20 November.

The saved feed says the 16 November resolved update was modified at 18:50 UTC. Its current later text attributes both pull-request events to storage read bandwidth and a disk setting; an earlier version is unavailable here.
The saved feed says the 13 November resolved update was modified at 21:45 UTC. Its current text includes the later account of both events; it cannot be treated as text published on 13 November.

Trellix reports observing 252 outage-themed emails across more than 30 organisations between approximately 17:04 and 20:38 Coordinated Universal Time. This is its observed sample, not a worldwide total.
Cofense published its account of an outage-themed message and Microsoft-like sign-in page; its description does not establish a successful compromise.
Trellix published its account of observed outage-themed emails and a sign-in chain. It says an asserted association with a named phishing kit remains unconfirmed.
KnowBe4 published telemetry ratios comparing 13 November outage-themed phishing with its 9–11 November baseline; these ratios concern its own product observations.
The department later reported a disruption affecting cargo lodgements as of approximately 09:12 Australian Eastern Daylight Time.
The department reported cargo lodgement services restored at 11:45 Australian Eastern Daylight Time; it described possible assessment delays and workarounds for affected lodgement references.
At 11:30 local time the council reported that online payments and applications were paused, with an in-person payment route remaining available.
The council stated online payments and applications would stay paused over the weekend pending service checks, despite improving upstream availability.
At 10:30 local time the council reported queued submissions were being processed; by its 14:00 update it reported online payment and application systems operating normally.

The Nelson Mandela Museum published a notice attributing an extension of two quotation deadlines to a 13 November Microsoft system outage or technical challenge; the revised deadline was noon on 17 November.
Cofense published its claim that outage-themed phishing bypassed three named email-security controls. Its report does not establish the exact message times or whether the outage caused a bypass.

2026-11-13T21:49:00Z — Anthropic marked its incident resolved, retrospectively giving an impact interval of 12 November 16:03 UTC to 13 November 16:40 UTC; it also said Microsoft recovery continued and occasional errors or delays could remain.
